title: North America capitals three of five · Cuba, Hispaniola and Jamaica
edition: North America capitals · Five regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the North America capitals, episode three of five. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
Four capitals of the great Caribbean islands: Cuba, Jamaica and the two halves of Hispaniola.

states.name: Havana
lines: Havana stands on the north coast of Cuba, on a bay that opens towards the Florida Straits.

Founded on its present site in 1519, it kept a walled Spanish city behind its ramparts for four centuries. Old Havana and its fortifications are a UNESCO site, and its Malecón, a seawall promenade of about eight kilometres, runs along the sea.
Remember Havana as the walled city on the bay, with the Malecón running along the sea.

states.name: Kingston
lines: Kingston stands on the south coast of Jamaica, across the harbour from the old pirate town of Port Royal.
Founded in 1692, after an earthquake sank Port Royal, it has one of the largest natural harbours in the world, and Bob Marley's home is now a museum here.
Remember Kingston as the harbour city that rose when the earthquake sank Port Royal.

states.name: Port-au-Prince
lines: Port-au-Prince stands on the bay of the same name, on the southern coast of Haiti.
Named for a French ship, Le Prince, that anchored in its bay, it was founded by the French in 1749; an earthquake in 2010 destroyed much of it.
Remember Port-au-Prince as the ship-named capital, founded in 1749 and largely rebuilt after the earthquake of 2010.

states.name: Santo Domingo
lines: Santo Domingo stands on the south coast of Hispaniola, on the island the Columbus family claimed first.
Its cathedral, finished in 1540, is the oldest in the Americas, and its Alcázar de Colón was the home of Diego Columbus, Christopher's son.
Remember Santo Domingo as the oldest cathedral in the Americas, and the house of Columbus's son.
states.transition: Let's bring Santo Domingo into view.

recap: Havana stands on the bay in the west, Kingston on the south coast of Jamaica, and Port-au-Prince and Santo Domingo share Hispaniola between them.
Remember the walled city and the Malecón, the harbour that rose when the earthquake sank Port Royal, the ship-named capital rebuilt after 2010, and the oldest cathedral in the Americas.
